The functor <MATH_0001> defined above
is a predeformation category.

We have to show that <MATH_0001> is (a) cofibred in groupoids over
<MATH_0002> and (b) that <MATH_0003> is a category equivalent
to a category with a single object and a single morphism.

<STRUCT_0001><STRUCT_0002>
Proof of (a). The fibre categories of <MATH_0004>
over <MATH_0005> are groupoids as the fibre categories
of <MATH_0006> are groupoids. Let <MATH_0007> be a morphism of
<MATH_0008> and let <MATH_0009> be an object of <MATH_0010>.
Because <MATH_0011> is fibred in groupoids, we can find a morphism
<MATH_0012> lying over <MATH_0013>. Since the composition
<MATH_0014> is equal the given map <MATH_0015> we see (by uniqueness
of pullbacks up to isomorphism) that the pullback via <MATH_0016>
of <MATH_0017> is <MATH_0018>, i.e., that there exists a morphism <MATH_0019>
lying over <MATH_0020> compatible with
<MATH_0021> and <MATH_0022>. This proves that <MATH_0023> has
pushforwards. We conclude by (the dual of)
Categories, Lemma <REF_0001>.

<STRUCT_0003><STRUCT_0004>
Proof of (b). If <MATH_0024>, then <MATH_0025> and since <MATH_0026>
is fibred in groupoids over <MATH_0027> we see that given any object
<MATH_0028> in <MATH_0029> the morphism <MATH_0030> is an isomorphism.
Hence every object of <MATH_0031> is isomorphic to <MATH_0032>.
Clearly the only self morphism of <MATH_0033> in <MATH_0034> is
the identity.
